description: Fetch and analyze recent GitHub Actions run logs via subagent dispatch to identify wasted effort and mistakes.

evals.name: Detect step boundaries in a synthetic log and confirm the dispatch gate
evals.prompt: I don't have live gh CLI access in this sandbox. Create a small synthetic GitHub Actions run log file (a few lines, containing at least 2 step markers in any of the formats the skill's Step 3 describes: flue skill markers, ##[group]/##[endgroup], or generic START/END), then follow the skill's Step 3 to detect step boundaries. Then follow Step 4 only up to the point of the dispatch-scope gate — state the AskUserQuestion you would ask (with the actual computed dispatch count) but do NOT actually dispatch any subagents.
evals.expected_output: Creates a synthetic log, runs (or correctly follows) scripts/find_step_boundaries.py to detect the step boundaries, and correctly states the dispatch-scope gate's AskUserQuestion with an accurate computed count before stopping — never silently proceeding to actual dispatch.
